The Barrio Boyzz was formed in 1991 by manager Joe Jacket, who proposed creating a mainstream Latino group.  They auditioned for chairman of EMI Records, Charles Koppelman, who signed the group to its sister label SBK Records.  The group's debut album, "Crazy Coolin'" (1992), failed to make any impact on music charts, but its lead single "Muy Suavemente" peaked at number 36 on the US "Billboard" Hot Latin Tracks chart. Released in 1984 and produced by group member Reggie Calloway, this album peaked at number seven on the R&B albums chart led by the number-one R&B single "Operator."  This single also scored the group their first (and to date, only) top-20 single on the pop charts, peaking at #18 in early 1985.
